problem:
Let ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ be eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ that correspond to eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=4$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=0,$ respectively.
What is the general solution of the matrix differential equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)?$

Let ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14067055/assets/72d318ad7ca3ea0dff8b598a3c7126fd48a48f25fb6bdfec859e91701ffb9d15.png) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14067055/assets/75c63b77244e0233dd11874e55a1ab674f6149d49b8fdd3c939afa1cf016ca6e.png) be eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ that correspond to eigenvalues $\lambda_1=-1$ and $\lambda_2=2,$ respectively.
What is the general solution of the matrix differential equation $\mathbf{x}'(t)=A\mathbf{x}(t)?$
examples.worked_solution:
Given a system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

$$
\mathbf{x}'(t)=A\mathbf{x}(t),
$$

where $A$ has two distinct eigenvalues ${\color{red}\lambda_1}, {\color{blue}\lambda_2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${\color{red}\mathbf{v}_1}$ and ${\color{blue}\mathbf{v}_2},$ the formula for the general solution is

$$
\mathbf{x}(t) = c_1{\color{red}\mathbf{v}_1} e^{{\color{red}\lambda_1} t} + c_2{\color{blue}\mathbf{v}_2} e^{{\color{blue}\lambda_2} t}, \qquad c_1,c_2 \in \mathbb{R}.
$$

Therefore, the general solution of our matrix differential equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$
